note: Re-judged 2026-11-03 by an independent auditor who authored none of 3a8eef5825 or 29f15481fa. RFC 9234 Section 5 read: "If a route is to be advertised to a Customer, a Peer, or an RS- Client (when the sender is an RS), and the OTC Attribute is not present, then when advertising the route, an OTC Attribute MUST be added with a value equal to the AS number of the local AS." The two moved units are internal/le/interoplab/bgp/check_rfc.go::checkOTCWithdrawal (both tags): 29f15481fa routes the three assertion-3 failures through a fail closure calling checkerFailure with the same ctx, lab, name, number 3 and cause, so every condition, message and assertion number is unchanged; 3a8eef5825 only corrects the positive tag's FRR version to 10.7.1, the lab's. The fixture change in 3a8eef5825 is what makes question 1 answerable: with local-role customer FRR's ingress rule (Section 5 ingress 3, "If a route is received from a Provider, a Peer, or an RS and the OTC Attribute is not present, then it MUST be added with a value equal to the AS number of the remote AS.") added OTC 65001 itself, the same value, so the old positive could not see a missing Ze stamp. With no FRR role the OTC 65001 FRR prints is the one parsed off Ze's wire, while Ze still treats FRR as a Customer: ze.conf configures role import provider and resolvePeerRole (otc.go) takes the configured role's complement when the peer sends no Role capability, as Section 4.2 says the locally configured role drives the procedures. The hand-written break otc_filter.go:204 (op.Code != otcAttrCode -> true), which stops the stamp while the route is still accepted and advertised, is recorded red at citation 3, so the interop positive now discriminates the stamp itself rather than the route's arrival. The negative half (route absent after the withdrawal, no attribute error, session up, assertions 4 onward) is byte-identical. All other carriers (the role package units and the role-otc .ci files with their exact C023040000FDE8 bytes) are unchanged and their judgement stands. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgements are in this file's git history.
